name: Brought Home
tagline: Half the people you know have eaten somewhere because of you.
epigraph: Two places go into this glass: a village in Mexico, and wherever you live.
glassware: a tall highball glass (about 300 ml), filled with ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. Line that lands: "the best night of a trip is sometimes the one after it, at your own table, telling it." Runner-up: "That's what you give them: the world, handed round, with directions." Horoscope check: one borderline sentence ("Not because you didn't love being there."), held by the one before it. Swap test clean against *Left Standing*, *For Good*, *Four Shares*, *Everybody's*. Echoes moved off: "what you rarely say" (*Not Only the Way*) → "Truth is"; "the people who didn't" (*Not Too Polite*) → "everyone who stayed"; "the nerve to try it" (creator-outlaw) → "with directions"; "stop apologising" (*The Other Berry*) dropped. whoYouAre cut from 200 to 150 words. Warnings accepted by Wren: "he" in yours 1–4 is Ron Cooper, never the guest; "in a tall glass" (overlap with caregiver-outlaw) is Hester's X9 wording for the build, not a motif. ✓
sources: Studio fact cards `_studio/fact-cards/del-maguey-oaxaca-old-fashioned.md` (Oxford COOPER, RON pdf 573–574, DEL MAGUEY MEZCAL pdf 638, 640; Robert Simonson, *A Proper Drink* p. 248; Ron Cooper, James Beard Foundation interview 2016 and *VinePair* podcast 2021, secondary, his words; Caskers listing for Chichicapa's 48%) and `_studio/fact-cards/paloma.md` (Oxford PALOMA pdf 1470; *Cocktail Codex* p. 212). Drink: *Flavor Matrix* honey pdf 148–149 (citrus its first pairing; mezcal on the chart, Smoke segment). Room notes: `work/explorer-regular-guy/`.
names_note: **Brought Home**, the room's pick (all three, r7): the story's own verb ("I brought it home and I started tasting it with friends") and what whoYouAre says the guest does. **Both Ways** is the runner-up, Tomás's pick until r6: going and coming home as one act, and the village one way, a street near home the other. The room moved off it because "wanting it both ways" is an idiom of reproach, the very sneer this person hides (Wren's flag). Also considered: *One Street Further*, *Where It's From* (Wren), *Come Back Tomorrow*, *Say Where*, *Two Addresses* (Tomás).
open_items: **Cooper's dates and the find (Hester C1, C3):** Oxford gives 1986 on holiday with friends (COOPER pdf 573) and 1990 at a café in Tlacolula (DEL MAGUEY pdf 638); *Proper* p. 248 has 1990 and an art project. The reading tells one scene, the holiday with friends that his own account matches, with no year; the café is dropped. He led the trip (his own words); the friends invited him.
**The border (C4):** his memory gives "1 liter", a narrated source "three-liter"; the reading says no number, and puts the border on a later trip ("Coming home from a later trip").

**Never "discovered" (C5):** Oxford uses it and quotes "It took an American… to discover" (pdf 640); kept out. His own saying ("you don't find mezcal, it finds you") rests on his word alone as "a famous Mexican dicho"; the reading gives it in his mouth ("He quotes a Mexican saying").

**Kept out on purpose:** the Paloma's Tlaquepaque "tourist attraction" line (beside the name *The Tourist* it reads as a sneer, and the full entry credits the Mexican American diaspora too); emigration and the saviour lines; the plant and bats (*Left Standing*); the salt rim (*Half a Rim*). The pinch of salt in the drink is Oxford's own seasoning and isn't mentioned in the reading.

**The honey (Tomás):** about three-quarters of the sugar; keep it equal parts honey and warm water (a 2:1 syrup goes OUT on sugar), and one teaspoon of lime (10 ml goes OUT on acid; Oxford uses half a lime). Any runny honey is the substitute; the reading never looks down on a supermarket jar. Its link to where the guest lives is our reading, not the *Matrix*'s.
**Grapefruit and medicines (Tomás, unsourced):** grapefruit interacts with some medicines. Not a veto; noted for Robin only.
**Chichicapa (Hester F25):** 48% per a Caskers listing, which says the ABV may vary; any village-labelled joven espadín mezcal of at least 40% is the substitute (swept 40–55%).
